Code generators

Source: R/codegen-utilities.R
code-generators.Rd

Code generators write routines as source files, as the classes of sympy.utilities.codegen: CCodeGen(), C89CodeGen(), C99CodeGen(), FCodeGen(), JuliaCodeGen(), OctaveCodeGen() and RustCodeGen(). Their methods (routine, write, dump_c, dump_h, dump_f95, dump_jl, dump_m, dump_rs, get_prototype, ...) are read with ast_attr(); the dump methods write to a connection. get_code_generator() returns the generator for a language, and codegen() writes the source files of named expressions.

Usage

CCodeGen(
  project = "project",
  printer = NULL,
  preprocessor_statements = NULL,
  cse = FALSE
)

C89CodeGen(
  project = "project",
  printer = NULL,
  preprocessor_statements = NULL,
  cse = FALSE
)

C99CodeGen(
  project = "project",
  printer = NULL,
  preprocessor_statements = NULL,
  cse = FALSE
)

FCodeGen(project = "project", printer = NULL)

JuliaCodeGen(project = "project", printer = NULL)

OctaveCodeGen(project = "project", printer = NULL)

RustCodeGen(project = "project", printer = NULL)

get_code_generator(language, project = NULL, standard = NULL, printer = NULL)

codegen(
  name_expr,
  language = NULL,
  prefix = NULL,
  project = "project",
  to_files = FALSE,
  header = TRUE,
  empty = TRUE,
  argument_sequence = NULL,
  global_vars = NULL,
  standard = NULL,
  code_gen = NULL,
  printer = NULL
)

Arguments

project

The project name.

printer

A code printer object, or NULL for the default.

preprocessor_statements

C preprocessor lines.

cse

Whether to eliminate common subexpressions.

language

"C", "C89", "C99", "F95", "JULIA", "OCTAVE" or "RUST".

standard

The C standard, for language "C".

name_expr

A list(name, expr) pair, or a list of them.

prefix

The file name prefix.

to_files

Whether to write files instead of returning them.

header, empty

Whether to write the header comment and empty lines.

argument_sequence, global_vars

As in make_routine().

code_gen

A code generator, instead of language.

Value

A code generator; codegen() returns a list of (file name, contents) pairs.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y")
res <- codegen(list("f", x * y), "C99", header = FALSE, empty = FALSE)
cat(res[[1]][[2]])
#> #include "f.h"
#> #include <math.h>
#> double f(double x, double y) {
#>    double f_result;
#>    f_result = x*y;
#>    return f_result;
#> }
